# SurveyBeat

## Ground rules

- Use glossary terms exactly: Pulse (not Survey), Person (not User), Round (not instance), Submission (not Response). Do not drift to the "avoid" synonyms.
- If a change contradicts an ADR, say so and add a new ADR under `docs/adr/`; never silently override one.
- Issues and specs live in GitHub issues (`gh`); conventions are in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. Commit subjects name the release slice, e.g. `R1 03: ...`.
- Privacy invariants are release blockers (SPEC §7): anonymous Submissions store no Person and no time (ADR 0005), comments are redacted at store time (ADR 0009), and every shown aggregate obeys the minimum group size (ADR 0004).

## Commands (from the repo root)

Node 24 (`.node-version`) and pnpm 12.18.0 are pinned.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck          # tsc -b with project references
pnpm typecheck:effect   # @effect/tsgo diagnostics; CI runs this first
pnpm lint               # oxlint --type-aware
pnpm format             # oxfmt; CI runs format:check
pnpm test               # Vitest "unit" project only
pnpm test:privacy       # Vitest "privacy" project only; NOT part of pnpm test
pnpm test <path>        # one file, e.g. pnpm test packages/domain/src/people/SignIn.test.ts
pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
```

CI runs `typecheck:effect`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, then the web build; the privacy suite is a separate required job. There is no root `dev` script: `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web dev` serves the UI only, and the app calls the API at `window.location.origin`. Exercise sign-in and end-to-end flows on a deployed stage.

## Layout and boundaries

- `packages/domain` — Effect schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `email/`); depends only on `effect`.
- `packages/api` — the `HttpApi` declaration shared by the Worker and the typed web client; depends on `domain`.
- `packages/cloudflare` — all Cloudflare adapters plus the `MainWorker` and `SubmissionWorker` entries; the only package that touches the Alchemy runtime.
- `apps/web` — one Vite project with two entries: the Foldkit app (`index.html`) and the plain-TypeScript answer page (`answer.html`).
- `packages/emails` — React Email templates and rendering. `packages/testing` — privacy harness. `infra` — Alchemy stack, scripts, Playwright e2e, privacy sweep. `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` — local lint rules.

## Toolchain traps

- Effect is 4.1.2, not 3.x. Import from `effect/Effect`, `effect/Schema`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/http/...`; there is no `@effect/platform` v3-style API here. Copy the import style from neighboring files.
- TypeScript 7 (native compiler) with `tsc -b`. A new package needs its own `tsconfig.json` and an entry in the root `tsconfig.json` references.
- Stricter than defaults: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type`), and relative imports carry explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
- Lint bans `any` and type assertions (`as Foo`) outside `*.test.ts` (`consistent-type-assertions: never`). Decode with Effect Schema or use typed helpers instead.
- All user-facing text comes from `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` or `packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts`; `no-literal-ui-text` fails otherwise. HTML shells must hold no visible text and an empty `<title>` (asserted in `messages.test.ts`). Plurals use `<base>.one`/`.other`.
- The lint plugin enforces the boundaries: `domain`/`api` may not import `cloudflare:*`, Alchemy, or Foldkit, and `apps/web/src/answer/**` may not import React, Base UI, Foldkit, or the HttpApi client.
- Keep the answer entry plain TypeScript within its budget (JS ≤ 10 KB gzip critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB); no framework, per ADR 0008.

## Tests

- Tests are colocated `*.test.ts`. A privacy test must be named `*.privacy.test.ts` or CI never runs it.
- Use `@effect/vitest` (`it.effect` for Effect programs).
- Adapter tests use `@alchemy.run/test`'s `Test.make({ dev: true })` against local workerd and are slow (deploy timeouts up to 240 s); run the single file you need.
- A new API endpoint must be classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` or the package will not typecheck; `registry.privacy.test.ts` checks the runtime declaration too.
- End-to-end tests run only against a deployed stage: `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app pnpm test:e2e` (install Chromium once with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium`).

## Infra

- Every Cloudflare resource is declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; no dashboard edits, no wrangler config.
- Run Alchemy from the repo root: the Organization DO migrations path (`packages/cloudflare/migrations`) is relative to the working directory. Build the web app first; the Main Worker serves `apps/web/dist`.
- `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-<name>` needs `WORKOS_API_KEY` and `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` in the environment. Who may create an Organization is `infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml`, per stage.
- Non-production stages never send real email; sends are recorded in D1's `captured_email`. Only `production` sends.
- The Submission Worker must keep every observability channel off. `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` reads the deployed settings back; the canary sweep proves no logs are kept. Stage scripts need `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- New SQL migrations: numbered files in `packages/cloudflare/migrations` (Durable Object) or `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations` (D1).

- [Cloudflare cf CLI](cloudflare-cf-cli.md) — authenticated cf CLI for SurveyBeat's Cloudflare account; discover commands with cf cli search
- [Wayfinder: always push and merge](wayfinder-always-push-merge.md) — push and squash-merge each resolved ticket's branch without asking
- [Merge own PRs](merge-own-prs.md) — squash-merge my green PRs in surveybeat-next without asking

# Comment themes are computed once at close, need two comments, never quote, and can't be edited

When a Round closes and meets the minimum group size, and the Organization has AI processing on (ADR 0015), the Organization Durable Object asks the model for at most 5 Comment themes over the Round's redacted comments (ADR 0009). Each theme is a short label and one neutral sentence. The model also returns which comments support each theme, and the object keeps only themes supported by **at least two comments**. The result is stored with the Round's Result and never recomputed.

**Who sees what.** Members see each theme's label and sentence, never raw comments and never counts. The Lead sees the themes, how many comments support each, and the redacted raw comments, as in Release 1. Comments that fit no theme with two supporters stay visible only to the Lead.

**No quotes.** The prompt and the JSON schema ask for paraphrase, and a check rejects any theme that repeats 6 or more consecutive words of a comment; a rejected theme is dropped, not repaired. Exact wording or a personal style can identify the author.

**Failure.** The call retries with backoff for up to 24 hours. Until it succeeds, Results show "Themes are being prepared"; after that, Results stand without themes. The Review window (#89) never waits for themes.

**No editing.** The Lead cannot edit, hide, or reorder themes. A Lead who could hide an unflattering theme before sharing would undercut trust before features (SPEC §3.1).

## Considered options

- **Themes from a single comment:** rejected. Shown to the whole Team, a one-comment theme is one person's words in other words.
- **Redacted quotes under each theme** (the old glossary wording): rejected for the same reason as quotes in the sentence.
- **Recomputing themes on view:** rejected. It would call the model on every view, could change what people already saw, and needs the comments sent again.

## Consequences

- The privacy rule table gains rows: a theme never shown below N, never with fewer than two supporting comments, never containing a 6-word run from a comment, and never shown to members with counts.
- Small Teams with few comments often get no themes; the Lead still has the raw comments.
- Themes exist only for Rounds that close after AI processing is turned on.
======
# The discussion guide is written by the AI, in the same call as the themes, for the Lead only

When a Round closes and meets the minimum group size, and the Organization has AI processing on (ADR 0015), the call that writes the Comment themes (ADR 0016) also writes the Round's discussion guide. It has four sections: what stood out, what people raised, Actions to check on, and at most 3 questions to ask the Team. A Round without comments still gets a guide from its scores and Actions.

**Input.** This extends ADR 0015's list of what may be sent: the Dimension scores and changes (with which are flagged as larger than usual), the redacted comments, the Question text, and the titles of open Actions passed through the same Redaction (ADR 0009). Never an Action owner, a Person, or any name, id, or time.

**Rules.** The guide never quotes (the 6-word-run check of ADR 0016 applies to every section), never says or guesses who said what, and must match a strict JSON schema. A guide that fails a check is dropped as a whole.

**No AI, no guide.** There is no rule-based fallback. With AI processing off, the Lead sees a line saying an Organization admin can turn it on. If the call fails for 24 hours, the Round has no guide.

**Lead only, as generated.** The guide is stored with the Result, generated once, shown only to the Lead on the Results page with a "Copy as text" button, and cannot be edited in SurveyBeat. After the conversation, the Lead can write a Note on the Results page that the Team sees.

## Considered options

- **Rules-written guide with optional AI questions:** rejected by the product owner; the guide is the AI's job.
- **A separate call for the guide:** rejected; it would send the comments twice.

## Consequences

- The guide exists only for Organizations that turn AI processing on, and only for Rounds that close afterwards.
- The privacy rule table gains rows for the guide: never below N, never shown to members, never containing a 6-word run from a comment, never naming an Action owner.

## 7. Quality requirements

- **Privacy tests are release blockers.** The suite proves at least the following. An anonymous submission has no stored path back to a person. Every result view respects the minimum group size, including subtraction across groups. Logs from the submission path contain no identifiers. Exports and the MCP server obey the same rules.
- **Performance.** The answer page reaches first paint (the screen with the anonymity statement) in under 1 second and shows the first Question's text in under 1.3 seconds, measured as the 75th percentile on a mid-range phone. The text needs one round trip, because the Invitation token is only in the URL fragment (ADR 0005, ADR 0008). Answer submission completes in under 300 ms at the 95th percentile. The results page renders in under 1.5 seconds for a team with two years of weekly rounds.
- **Reliability.** No invitation is sent twice. No invitation is skipped silently. Failed sends show up in the lead's view with the reason.
- **Accessibility.** WCAG 2.2 AA on every page. The answer flow works with a screen reader and with a keyboard alone.
- **Testing approach.** Test behavior through the domain services and the API, not internal functions. Swap Effect layers for in-memory adapters in unit tests. Run a small set of end-to-end tests against a real preview stage, covering create pulse, receive invitation, answer from email, close round, see results, and create action.

content.text:
## Scoping brief: issue #103 (R2 02: themes and discussion guide at Round close)

**Scoper note:** The coordinator asked for a shorter report and skipped item 1 because the main session has already read the close and compute code. Item 1 is therefore covered only briefly below. The task is complex. It touches the DO, domain, API, privacy registry and a new AI call path, and it has a retry/backoff requirement that the existing job code does not meet (see Risks). Please read the key files named here yourself before planning.

## Goal
When a Round closes at or above N, with `aiProcessing` on, the Organization DO makes one AI call. The call produces at most 5 Comment themes and a Lead-only discussion guide. Both are validated, stored with the Result once, and never recomputed. `RoundResult` gains a members' `themes` view and Lead-only fields. Failures retry with backoff for up to 24 h. The Results view must respect the privacy rules.

## Acceptance criteria
Copied from the issue:
- One model call per Round, scheduled by the Round lifecycle after the Result is computed. Retry with backoff for up to 24 h through the schedule table, then the Round has neither themes nor guide.
- Prompt plus strict JSON schema. At most 5 themes (label, one neutral sentence, supporting comment indexes). Guide has four sections and at most 3 questions.
- Checks before storing: drop a theme with fewer than 2 supporting comments; drop a theme that repeats 6+ consecutive words of a comment; drop the whole guide if any section fails. Store once; never recompute.
- Not run when the Round is below N or AI processing is off. Rounds closed before AI was turned on get nothing.
- `RoundResult` gains `themes` (members see label and sentence). Lead-only fields (support counts, guide) go only to the Lead. Classify in `PrivacyRegistry.ts`.

Tests from the issue: domain tests for the checks; lifecycle test with the fake `AiClient` covering success, retry, give-up after 24 h, AI off, and below N; privacy rule-table rows from ADR 0016 and 0019.

Added by me, not in the issue: the ADR 0016/0019 "privacy rule table" is referenced but not written down anywhere. Rules R1–R11 exist only as code comments in `Results.ts` and `Results.test.ts`. The issue's rows therefore have no existing home to extend.

## Relevant code

**1. Close lifecycle and schedule table (Organization DO)**
- `packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.ts:770` `executeCloseJob` closes the Round and inserts a `compute` job with `dueAt: now`, then runs it inline. The Result-computation path is at `:809` `executeComputeJob`, and the Result is saved at `:854`.
- Compute failure handling is at `:898–926`. It counts attempts in the job payload (`parseAttempts`, `:91`). After 3 attempts it saves a "delayed" Result. Below 3 it only updates the payload and does not move `dueAt`, so the retry is immediate, not backed off.
- `:932` `runDueJobs` loops over `rounds.getDueJobs(now)` and dispatches by job type. `:961` is the `alarm` handler. `:168` `repairAlarm` arms the alarm to the earliest pending job.
- Schedule table DDL: `packages/cloudflare/migrations/0006_rounds.sql:61`. Columns are `id, round_id, type IN ('open','close','compute','send','remind'), due_at, status IN ('pending','running','completed','cancelled'), payload, created_at, completed_at`. Adding an AI job type needs a CHECK change, which means a new migration.
- Latest migration: `0011_ai_processing.sql`, so the next is `0012`.

**2. RoundResult shape and API**
- Schema: `packages/domain/src/rounds/Results.ts:126–147`. Fields include `questions: QuestionResult[]` (`text` at `:98`, `change` and `typicalChange` per question, `trend`), `dimensions: DimensionResult[]` (`score`, `contributors` optional, `change` with `highlight`), and `comments: CommentResult[]` (`questionVersionId`, `text`, at `:115–119`).
- "Larger than usual" is `Highlight` (`Results.ts:40–47`), produced by `evaluateHighlight` (`:262`). It appears on question and dimension changes.
- Built by `calculateRoundResult` (`Results.ts:345–362`). Comments are shuffled (`shuffleComments`, `:278`) and masked below round N (`:1089–1098`).
- Stored via `SqlRounds.ts:828` `saveRoundResult` and `:842` `getRoundResult`, as a JSON payload in `round_result` (`0009_results.sql`), decoded at `SqlRounds.ts:192`.
- Endpoint: `packages/api/src/index.ts:331` `rounds.getResults` at `GET /teams/:teamId/rounds/:roundId/results`. Handler is `packages/cloudflare/src/RoundHandlers.ts:125–127`, which calls `viewResults` with `currentMember`.
- Role logic is in the DO at `packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.ts:1382–1490`. Authorization uses `authorizeRoundAction(..., "team.viewResults")`. Rounds that are scheduled or open return only the response count (`:1417`). Closed, ready or shared Rounds read the stored Result (`:1443`), or compute it in place if missing. The Result is then passed through `enforceEffectiveNOnResult` (`:1474`). Non-Leads have `comments` set to `[]` (`:1478–1483`), so a members' view check happens here.
- Hook point for `themes` and Lead-only fields: this same block, `:1474–1490`.

**3. Actions and title redaction**
- Actions are stored in the DO table `action` (`packages/cloudflare/migrations/0010_actions.sql`). `title TEXT NOT NULL`, with `owner_id`.
- Domain: `packages/domain/src/actions/Action.ts:14–50`. `ActionRecord.title` is `NonEmptyString`. `ActionItem` adds `ownerEmail`.
- SQL: `packages/cloudflare/src/SqlActions.ts`. `:123` inserts and `:143` updates `title` as-is. Nothing redacts it.
- Redaction function: `packages/domain/src/privacy/Redaction.ts:185` `redact(text, roster)`. It is called at store time only, in `packages/cloudflare/src/SqlRounds.ts:642` and `:684` for comments. Action titles would need the same call before they reach the AI input. This is an open question: ADR 0019 says titles pass through the same Redaction, but nothing currently does that.

**4. AiClient, adapter, wiring, and the aiProcessing setting**
- Interface: `packages/domain/src/ai/AiClient.ts`. `RedactedText` brand (`:8–12`). `AiInput` (`:16–41`) has questions, comments and actions. `AiRequest` has `instructions`, `input`, `schemaName`, `schema`, `maxTokens` (`:44–50`). Errors are `AiNotConfigured`, `AiRejected` and `AiUnavailable`. The Context service is at `:73`.
- Fake: `packages/domain/src/ai/testing.ts`. `fakeAiClient(responses)` returns `{layer, requests}`. It dies if called more times than scripted.
- Adapter: `packages/cloudflare/src/ai/OpenRouterAiClient.ts`. `makeOpenRouterAiClient` (`:137`) retries 408/429/502/503, timeouts and network errors, up to 3 times. `OpenRouterAiClientLive` (`:191`) reads `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.
- **Not wired.** `OpenRouterAiClientLive` is not referenced by any layer. `MainWorker.ts` and `Organization.ts` never provide `AiClient`. `infra/alchemy.run.ts` has no `OPENROUTER` binding. The Organization DO would need an `AiClient` layer and a secret binding.
- `aiProcessing` in DirectoryState: `packages/domain/src/people/Directory.ts:53`. Set on update at `:452` and `:501`. Read from D1-less DO SQL in `packages/cloudflare/src/SqlDirectory.ts:51–66` (from `organization.ai_processing`, migration `0011`). Also read from `SqlRounds.ts:787–791`. `Organization.ts:471` passes it to the invitation and reminder emails.

**5. PrivacyRegistry**
- `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts`. Every endpoint is a key `"group.endpoint"` in `privacyRegistry`, typed against `EndpointKey<typeof SurveyBeatApi>`. Each entry is either `{_tag: "NoResultData", why: string}` or `{_tag: "ResultData", inputs: Arbitrary}`.
- `rounds.getResults` is `ResultData` with `roundResultScenarios` (`:74–75`). `RoundResultScenario` is at `:60`. Its `Arbitrary` generator drives a property test.
- The matching check is `packages/api/src/registry.privacy.test.ts`. It requires that every endpoint is classified, that there are no stale keys, and that every `ResultData` endpoint has a responder. The responder builds the Result the way the handler does and runs `violations(...)`. This test will need to change if `themes` or the guide become Result-bearing fields.

**6. Privacy tests**
- Files: `packages/cloudflare/src/SubmissionWorker.privacy.test.ts`, `packages/cloudflare/src/Submissions.privacy.test.ts`, `packages/api/src/registry.privacy.test.ts`, `packages/domain/src/privacy/Redaction.privacy.test.ts`, `packages/domain/src/rounds/Results.privacy.test.ts`, `packages/testing/src/Unlinkability.privacy.test.ts`.
- `Results.privacy.test.ts` uses named invariants P1–P5: subtraction (P1), unlinked comments (P2), a 50-round property test (P3), role access (P4, admin and outsiders get nothing), and open rounds hiding everything (P5). It calls `calculateRoundResult` directly, with no DO.
- `Submissions.privacy.test.ts` uses A1–A9 and inspects the SQL schema, for example that anonymous tables are `WITHOUT ROWID`.
- No existing privacy test drives the DO or a stored Result end to end. The new theme and guide rows would be the first. For the "Lead only" rule, look at P4 and the `isLead` branch in `Organization.ts:1478`.
- ADR 0016 and 0019 "privacy rule table" rows: no table file exists in `SPEC.md` (§7 at `:236` has no table) or `docs/`. The implementer would need to decide where the rows live.

**7. Lifecycle tests**
- `packages/domain/src/rounds/Lifecycle.test.ts:143` `it.effect("simulates skip, pause, close, and cancel using Effect TestClock")`. This is domain only.
- `packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.test.ts`. It is a single test (`:159`, "Round lifecycle engine: alarm points at earliest due job…"). It drives the DO through `RoundTestRoutes.ts` (HTTP, `:105–231`). It uses `organization.runScheduleJob(closeJob.id, closeJob.due_at)` and `getAlarm()` and `getEarliestPendingJobDueAt()`. It checks close idempotence and reads `getRoundResult`.
- `packages/cloudflare/src/ResultsStorage.test.ts` covers `saveRoundResult` and decoding. `ActionsApi.test.ts` covers the Action API.
- No existing test covers retry timing or 24 h give-up. Time is driven by passing `nowMs` to `runScheduleJob`, not by a TestClock, on the DO side.

## Scope
- Change: a new `ai` job type in the schedule table (new migration `0012`). An AI step in the close and compute path, guarded by `aiProcessing` and N. Checks (2-supporter, 6-word run, schema) in the domain. `themes` and Lead-only guide fields on `RoundResult` and `getResults`. Privacy registry update. Tests as listed above.
- Leave alone: the answer page, the Submission Worker, email templates, the Review window (#89), and the Note feature.

## Validation
- Focused: `pnpm test packages/domain/src/rounds/Results.test.ts`, `pnpm test packages/domain/src/ai`, `pnpm test packages/cloudflare/src/ai/OpenRouterAiClient.test.ts`, `pnpm test packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.test.ts` (adapter test, slow), `pnpm test packages/api/src/registry.privacy.test.ts`.
- Privacy: `pnpm test:privacy` (not part of `pnpm test`).
- Typecheck: `pnpm typecheck:effect` then `pnpm typecheck`.
- End-to-end: a user-facing change, so it needs a deployed stage. `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app pnpm test:e2e`. The stage needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set, or the AI path fails closed.

## Risks and unknowns
1. **Retry is not backed off.** Existing compute retries have no `dueAt` change and run immediately, up to 3 attempts. The 24 h backoff needs a new retry mechanism in the schedule table.
2. **AiClient is not provided to the DO.** The adapter exists, but the layer and the `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` binding are missing.
3. **Action titles are not redacted** before they would reach the AI input (ADR 0019 requires it).
4. **Privacy rule table has no home.** The ADR rows have nowhere to go yet.
5. **The members' view of themes.** The issue says members see label and sentence only. The `CommentResult` shape currently carries `questionVersionId` and `text`, and the new `themes` shape is undefined. The "Themes are being prepared" state needs a representation in `RoundResult` or the API response, which is not decided.
6. **Schema compatibility.** `RoundResult` is stored as JSON and decoded in `SqlRounds.ts:192`. Adding fields needs optional keys, as `DimensionResult.contributors` already does (`Results.ts:65`).

## Possible split
- **Slice A (domain, no DO):** `packages/domain/src/ai/` checks and the theme and guide schema, plus `packages/domain/src/rounds/Results.ts` `RoundResult` additions. Its tests are the domain check tests. No dependencies.
- **Slice B (DO schedule and job):** `packages/cloudflare/migrations/0012_*.sql`, `packages/cloudflare/src/SqlRounds.ts` (job types and retry), `packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.ts` (the AI step after compute). Depends on A for the types.
- **Slice C (Results view and API):** `packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.ts:1382–1490`, `packages/cloudflare/src/RoundHandlers.ts`, `packages/api/src/index.ts` and `PrivacyRegistry.ts`, `registry.privacy.test.ts`. Depends on A.
- **Slice D (wiring and privacy tests):** `packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts` and `infra/alchemy.run.ts` for the `AiClient` layer and secret, plus privacy tests. Depends on B and C.
